messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aleks Novak <alek.novak@edgeai.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: burst SLO scenario walkthrough & next steps

Hi Danielle —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and what I promised to follow up with:

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Target p50 latency for 256-token responses: <= 120ms (interactive UI)
- Target p95 latency under normal traffic: <= 320ms
- Target throughput: sustained 800 requests/minute with short bursts to ~2,400 reqs/min for 3–5 minutes
- Concurrency target: typical 40 concurrent requests, spike to 200 concurrent during peak campaigns
- Streaming requirement: server-sent events (chunked) with first-chunk < 100ms and steady chunk cadence for long responses

Immediate asks you had:
1) SLO acceptance criteria we can run in a joint validation (latency/throughput/concurrency)
2) SOC 2 evidence + any IP/data residency questions
3) Procurement timeline for PO and whether we need an NDA or MSA up front

Attached: a draft SLO worksheet that maps the targets above to test scenarios (slo_worksheet.xlsx). I also included a lightweight mutual action plan we can iterate on.

Proposed next steps:
- Rafael + Karthik to propose a short validation runbook and required environment (by EOD Monday)
- Acme to confirm preferred week for a 2-hour joint test window (we suggested Oct 12 or Oct 19)
- Procurement to share PO timing and any contract redlines

If useful I can loop in Marissa (solutions) and Grace (customer success) to own the operational checklist and rollout plan.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachments: slo_worksheet.xlsx

From: Danielle Park <dpark@acmehealth.com>

Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: burst SLO scenario walkthrough & next steps

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the clear recap and for the worksheet — appreciate it. A few clarifications from our side:

- The p50/p95 numbers are fine. For p99 we’d like to see an upper bound of 800ms for normal traffic; anything above that must trigger fallback behavior to our cached responses.
- For burst behavior: our marketing campaigns historically run two types of bursts — short micro-bursts (1–2 minutes) up to ~3,000 reqs/min and longer sustained spikes (10–20 minutes) up to ~1,200 reqs/min. Our primary ask is that tail latency (p95/p99) remains under the thresholds during the first 60–90 seconds of the burst.
- Streaming: first-chunk timing is critical for perceived responsiveness — good to see you call that out.

Procurement: I’ve copied procurement team; we’ll check on PO windows. We’ll also attach our security questionnaire and a copy of the last internal SOC audit for your records (sending in a separate email).

For the joint validation runbook, Oct 12 is our preference (midday PT). Please include necessary test harness details — e.g., can you provide a JMeter/Locust config or do we need to run our internal generator?

Thanks,
Danielle
Danielle Park | SRE Lead, Acme Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: burst SLO scenario walkthrough & next steps

Thanks Rafael — mapping out the technical runbook here. High level:

Validation objectives:
- Verify p50/p95/p99 across steady-state and burst shapes (we’ll collect server-side token-level latency and request-level tail metrics)
- Confirm streaming first-chunk < 100ms at p95 for 256-token responses
- Observe autoscale time-to-capacity (cold -> warm pool -> fully provisioned) and queueing behavior when bursts exceed warm pool capacity

Proposed test harness & metrics:
- We will supply a Locust configuration (attached as a gist link) that replicates your client patterns. If you prefer your in-house generator, send the load profile and we’ll adapt.
- Required telemetry: server-side traces, token timing (first token delivered), queue depth, warm-pool occupancy, GPU utilization, and model-variant fallback events. We’ll provide a Grafana dashboard template.

Warm pool / autoscale behavior to demonstrate:
- Start with a pre-warmed pool sized for ~40 concurrent sessions.
- Trigger micro-burst (3k rpm) and observe first 90s tail behavior; show fallback to cached responses if p99 exceeds 800ms.
- Measure scale-up time from baseline to handling 200 concurrent sessions and from warm pool to full provision. Expectation: <90s to reach warm-pool-backed capacity, <180s to reach full provisioning in our standard config; we will show these numbers in the run.

Data/ops needs from Acme:
- Test API key and a short allowlist (IP ranges) or temporary VPC peering instructions if you want traffic from our test harness to run inside your network.
- A small set of representative prompts (we only need 50 unique prompt variants) to reproduce realistic token distributions.

Deliverables before the run (we’ll provide by Monday EOD unless you ask for earlier):
- Locust config + run instructions (or adapt to your generator)
- Grafana dashboard + metrics collection plan
- Short readout template we’ll use to capture SLO pass/fail and recommended next actions

Happy to jump on a 30-min prep call Tuesday to walk through the runbook.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: (Locust config gist link)

This looks great and very actionable. We confirm Oct 12 at 11:00 PT for a 2-hour window. Procurement will send PO terms pending SOC 2.

Action items on our side:

- We’ll provide a temporary allowlist IP range for the test harness; VPC peering is not required for the validation run.

One question on fallback behavior: when you fallback to cached responses, will you provide a header or response flag we can assert in the validation script so we can differentiate real vs fallback responses in our logs? If yes, we’ll include that assertion in our pass/fail criteria.

Thanks — Danielle
